Msamati's performance as Sam is perfect.
'Master Harold' takes a while to rouse itself from its elegant torpor – but it does so, and powerfully.
Msamati delivers a performance of enormous power and grace, of lightness and depth. A master at work.
I was impressed and often moved by it, but I also found myself thinking: why this? Why now?
The ever-astonishing Lucian Msamati gives one of the year's best performances.
The production may be a slow-burn initially, but it ignites with an overpowering power that is shattering.
He is such a wonderful actor, really one of our very best, and he is magnificent here, quietly registering every moment of feeling.
The revival is lifted by two brilliant performances by Lucian Msamati and Hammed Animashaun as Sam and Willie.
Athol Fugard's masterly semi-autobiographical play MASTER HAROLD AND THE BOYS makes a welcomed return to London after 36 years but with a wrong production in the wrong theatre.

cn.t: Fugard's powerful, semi-autobiographical apartheid drama receives a taut, elegant revival with dignified performances from Msamati and Animashaun, though some find the symbolism heavy-handed and the National Theatre an ill-suited venue.
